topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the course structure, target audience, and key learning objectives for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Biological principles of carcinogenesis and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer arises from accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations that cause a breakdown in normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and progression from benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distinguishing histological and clinical features of benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard pathological naming rules and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms across tissue types.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological disruptions, systemic effects, and metastatic complications that cause disease and death in cancer patients.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence in humans alongside cancer occurrence across diverse animal species and multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and applications of clinical cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale, histological basis, and clinical efficacy and limitations of screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic reviews the learning outcomes and provides closing logistical reminders for upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
